main:1.text: Surviving Fimbulwinter is one of the goals in God of War Ragnarök. It is the first goal in The Path. It mostly serves as a tutorial and setting up important plot points. Three years after fulfilling Faye's last wish, Kratos and Atreus prepare for the soon-to-come Ragnarök. While Kratos guilts his wife's loss, Atreus secretely investigates his persona as Loki.

main:2.text: The Quest for Týr is one of the goals in God of War Ragnarök. It is the second goal in The Path. We have arrived in Svartalfheim. The Dwarves have left us far from Niðavellir. We will journey by boat. The Dwarves in Niðavellir are not welcoming. To find Durlin, we must find someone who will speak to us.

main:3.text: Old Friends is one of the goals in God of War Ragnarök. It is the third goal in The Path and the first where Atreus is fully playable, and the first to have Jörmungandr's appearance. Sindri thinks our first stop should be Jörmungandr, but I haven't seen him since Fimbulwinter started. Hope he's out there somewhere, staying warm... Jörmungandr said "iron wood." What could that mean...?

main:4.text: Much has changed since last we were in Alfheim. We must travel through the  Temple of Light to reach Gróa's shrine. Gróa deceived Odin; Ragnarök does not lead to the destruction of all. There is much to consider from the prohecy we saw, but now we must find a way out of this realm. War has come again to Alfheim. We must fight our way back to the gateway.

main:5.text: Angrboda seems to know a lot about me. Says if I follow her, I'll get my answers. I just need to keep up... Angrboda wants to show me a new shrine. Wonder whose... I still feel kinda messed up. Angrboda wants my help with some "Giant stuff." I know she's just trying to take my mind off the future... and maybe it's working a little.

main:6.text: We head to Vanaheim. Freya may yet try to kill me, but I will help her break the spell that binds her to Midgard. If this is how she collects her "blood payment," I will honor it. Freya is bound by something in this realm. We will find it and destroy it. Mimir is asking to speak with Freya's brother, Freyr.

main:7.text: I am in such. Huge. Trouble. And I'm freezing... I need to get somewhere warm. Fast. Chaurli! Glad to see him, but he needs help. I gotta look around the house to see if there's anything I can use to get him warm. A fire should help. Freya left lots of stuff in here----there has to be fuel I can use to light something and get Chaurli warm.

main:8.text: Thor and I have traveled to Muspelheim. Time to find a piece of this mask... I saw Surtr's shrine that we found last time I was here with Father. I've gotta get back to it, open it up, and find out the secret prophecy inside. Sure was nice to see Angrboda again. I'm glad to see her exploring outside Jötunheim. Now I just need to get back to Thor and find that mask piece.

main:9.text: The Word of Fate is one of the goals in God of War Ragnarök. It is the ninth goal in The Path, the player will now be Kratos again. Hoping the Norns can help provide the answers needed, it's time to travel to Midgard with Freya.

main:10.text: Forging Destiny is one of the goals in God of War Ragnarök. It is the tenth goal in The Path. Kratos explains his intent to kill Heimdall, causing Brok and Sindri to gather the Draupnir ring and visit "The Lady". Sindri attempts to join Kratos, but the annoyed latter orders Brok to come, to Sindri's dismay.

main:12.text: Reunion is one of the goals in God of War Ragnarök. It is the twelfth goal in The Path. We must venture to Helheim to correct Atreus' mistake Perhaps the the squirrel can help us The Hel-hound, Garm, has been unleashed upon the realms. Atreus and I just find the creature and stop it. My son's mistakes weigh heavily on him I wish it were not so, but in this regard, he is like his father.

main:13.text: Creatures of Prophecy is one of the goals in God of War Ragnarök. It is the thirteenth goal in The Path. Freyr and the Light Elf, Byggvir, have been captured by Odin's forces. As Freyr's allies work to rescue them, Hildisvíni has asked us to seek the wolves who chase the sun and moon, Sköll and Hati, as they too are missing. We have seen in prophecy the moon taken by Einherjar.

main:14.text: Some time after driving back Odin's forces in Vanaheim, Kratos and Atreus head back to Sindri's House. There, they find Freyr being nursed back to health by Freya, although Freyr's quite out of it. Atreus can have a proper chat with the pair, until Kratos calls everyone to the dining table. At the table, Kratos slams Gjallarhorn down, marking Heimdall's defeat.

main:15.text: Enough running. We will find Sindri. We will see to our friend.

main:16.text: Surtr is a blacksmith, like the Dwarves... Dwarf. We search for a forge. Atreus is confident this ashen man is the one we seek. We follow Surtr. He says he will "become our monster."

main:17.text: On the eve of battle, the most important preparation one can do is rest. I do not know how much sleep will come to me this night, but I will try. The time has come. We have prepared. Now to blow the the horn... Odin's War Machines are our greatest threat. We must fight our way to them.

main:18.text: The realms are safe. For now. But there is much to do, much destruction to repair. Freya, Mimir, and I will see to it together. Beyond Ragnarök starts automatically in Midgard, after finishing the story. The game doesn't list proper objectives for this quest, so it can be a bit confusing what to do. If you reached this point you will already have seen the credits at the end of the previous mission.

side:1.text: Ratatoskr has asked us to return the Stags of the Four Seasons to the Realm Between Realms. Even though this problem is his doing, we will stay alert for any we encounter on our journey. The squirrel has given us feed that will help lead the stags back to where they belong.

side:2.text: Lúnda is planning to honor Brok's memory at Ræb's tavern in Svartalfheim. We will attend and pay our respects. We will say our final goodbye to Brok at the Sverd Sands. It is at the end of the ferry closest to the pretender Týr's prison. We can track the location on our compass.

side:3.text: A Draugr unlike any other we have ever faced spawns from holes in the ground This monster must be put down and the scars on the land must be healed. This sidequest requires you to first defeat one of The Hateful. The first you can find is in Svartalfheim behind The Watchtower, a hidden location near Bay of Bounty's Mystic Gateway and Sindri's workstation. Upon defeating The Hateful, the questline kicks off.

side:4.text: Countless died in the disaster that created the crater in Vanaheim. One such soul can not move on to Fólkvangr without their hourglass. Were we to return it, we may learn more about what caused the disaster in the first place. The spirit remembers a place with three waterfalls in The Sinkholes. That is where we will find their remains.

side:5.text: Restless spirits roam the massive crater at the center of Vanaheim. They seem to know of the disaster that created it. If we can return one such spirit's brooch, we may learn what happened that day. The spirit met their end at a vista with a fallen pillar somewhere in the plains.

side:6.text: A spirit in the Vanaheim crater has unfinished business. In life, they failed to deliver a scroll to their superior. Perhaps we can solve that problem in death. The spirit mentioned a grove of red tress in The Plains is where we can find their remains.

side:7.text: Not every day one needs to fetch a mead stein for a lost spirit, but these are unusual times. The spirit mentioned a location between three bodies of water in The Plains.

side:8.text: The Vanir turned to Seidr magic to use against the Einherjar. Their corruption must be put to rest. The Seidr fanatics are slain. I will tell the spirit her mistake was corrected.

side:9.text: Odin appointed a new Queen of the Valkyries. We will end this pretender's reign.

side:10.text: There are graves across the realms that react to the presence of the hilt we found in Midgard Placing Skofnung inside summons the souls of Berserkers who defend their king, even in death. Formidable as they are, we will prove we are their better.

side:11.text: We may not have survived were it not for Birgir. He is alive and in need of our help. The dragon that stranded us in the rater appears to be guarding his position. The dragon guarding Birgir's position is now dead, and Birgir is safe. We should speak  to him and see if he needs further aid. Our Key of Yggdrasial can provide Birgir safe passage back to Freyr's Camp. We owe him a debt for what he did on the boat.

side:12.text: Freya seeks to remedy something from her past. The site of her wedding with Odin is our destination. We will explore the wedding site and help Freya confront her past. Freya has found some measure of acceptance. There is nothing left for us in this shrine.

side:13.text: There may be more to the statue of Freyr here in the desert. It could be worth investigation. Socketing the crystals may restore light to the desert... which might provide unexpected benefits. There may be unforeseen benefits to our task. We should investigate the stones.

side:14.text: Poison corrupts the spirit's garden. WE must destroy them to bring life back to the land. We will speak to the spirit. She should know her garden grows once more.

side:15.text: The Guiding Light Set is an armor set found in God of War Ragnarök. The armor pieces can be found during the course of the Guiding Light Favor, which can be started by finding one of the pieces. The gauntlets can be found to the northwest of Týr's Temple, around the back of Sindri's shop. The breastplate can be found inside the helmet from Týr's statue on the Lake of Nine.

side:16.text: Releasing Garm has had consequences. Realm tears have opened, allowed Hel-Walkers into other realms. Atreus and Freya can seal these tears if given time. We will correct this mistake.

side:17.text: We found one corpse, but that is not enough to go on. Finding other corpses could help us narrow down where the Soul Eater hides. We have an idea of where the Soul Eater is hiding. The first strike is ours for the taking.

side:18.text: Modvitnir's Rig can be found on the island with the giant crane at its center The crane itself may be worth investigating. Radsvinn's Rig is on an island infested with monsters. It would be best to stay on guard when approaching the rig there. Althjof's Rig is on an island with a giant gantry running through it. The gantry may prove useful while we scout the island.

side:19.text: Despite the effects of Fimbulwinter, flowers still bloom across the nine realms. Freya spoke too much about these flowers and her desire to collect them while Atreus was away. I do remember Freya had an affinity for a white-petaled flower whose name I cannot recall.

side:20.text: There are massive tremors in the plains that do not seem natural. We could investigate.

side:21.text: Odin built this dam to dry out the people of Vanaheim who lived here before. We can put an end to it. First we make our way inside. A crank seems to control the walls of the dam. We can use it to flood the crater.

side:22.text: The animal from Freyr's Camp, Helka, is tracking a scent. She seems to want us to follow. Helka has lead us to a spot where we can launch Skidbladnir. It appears Birgir survived his fall, but is likely injured. We should seek his location.

side:23.text: We look for the creature that Atreus "heard" cry out in pain. The sandstorm makes navigation difficult. We should seek shelter. The creature appears trapped somewhere in the caves beneath the desert. The Hafgufa is bound to this canyon by hive tendrils. Destroying them may may allow it to free itself.

side:25.text: A storm ragesin the East as it did in the West before freeing the Hafgufa. We must find the cave entrance to free the creature. Another Hafgufa is somewhere in this cave. We must find it to clear the sandstorm. The Hafgufa is bound to the hive matter, same as the last. We will free it before making our way back to the surface.

side:26.text: Durlin wishes for a small hammer near a giant Dwarf statue in the bay. This hammer appears to be a symbol to the Dwarves. After everything they have endured at the hands of Odin any hope we can give them is worth our efforts. Durlin's hammer was sealed inside the much larger hammer of the giant Dwarf statue. He and the rest of the Dwaves will be grateful when we return it to him at the tavern.

side:27.text: Perhaps the largest piece of Asgard landed in Niflheim, off the path to the raven's tree I am curious to see where this new path might lead.

side:28.text: Another flying dragon ambushed us as we made our way through the sinkholes. Although different from the dragon we encountered while tracking Birgir, we will slay it all the same. If we wish to follow it, we must get through the gate it flew over.

side:29.text: Completing it is required to open the Nornir chest in the Crucible. We discovered half of a Realm Seed to Muspelheim. When we visited the realm winters ago, we found challenges that tested our strength and skill If we wish to return, we should seek the other half of the seed. With both halves of the Muspelheim Realm Seed in our possession, we can now visit The Crucible at our leisure.

side:30.text: Mimir spoke with the Elves, Beyla and Byggvir, while in  Freyr's Camp They spoke of an Elven Sanctum of forbidden knowledge, deep in the Eastern desert of Alfheim. It may contain valuable resources for our journey. I am not sure exactly what it is we seek, but it is likely important to both Light and Dark Elves. We should expect it to be defended. The Consul's journal is sealed.

side:31.text: The Eyes of Odin is one of the favors in God of War Ragnarök. Odin's Ravens are green spectral birds that act as Odin's eyes and ears throughout the nine realms. While you don't get anything for killing them there on the spot, hitting certain milestones will unlock the Legendary Chests at the base of The Raven Tree in Niflheim to unlock exclusive Armor and Runic Attacks.

side:32.text: It is unlocked after opening the Nornir chest in Muspelheim and inspecting the new Surtr's Sword that appears. New challenges await inside the Muspelheim Crucible. We should revisit the initial arenas to continue to test our abilities. Completing different combinations of these challenges seems to unlock a set of Final Challenges in the main arena.

side:33.text: Wreckage from Asgard's destruction has landed across the Nine Realms. Einherjar soldiers, still loyal to Odin, have made camp in the remnants of their realm. If left alone, they may reorganize and cause more problems for a world trying to heal. We will send them back to Valhalla.

side:34.text: Ratatoskr has provided us with a trap to capture the Lindwyrms. It sits on his bench outside of Sindri's house. To begin this Favor, you must first complete The Word of Fate main quest in Midgard. Once you've done this, return to Sindri's House on the world tree and talk to Ratatoskr. He'll be at his usual spot to the left of Sindri's House.

side:35.text: The spirit told us of riches on Alberich Island. It would benefit us to collect them. Alberich Hollow is said to have treasure waiting deeper within. Let us secure it. The Spirit seeks to know the fate of his son. We will find him... or what is left of him.

side:36.text: Lúnda speaks of an orb she wants returned. She did not say more about the orb's origin or intended use. We have found the orb she seeks. It feels lightweight, but not fragile. It does not appear to be of value or have clear practical application. Maybe it contains magic?

side:37.text: It appears Mimir was not a friend to the Dwarves of Svartalfheim. He tells us this island is home to a prisoner, and we must find a key. Mimir now requests we take the key to a watchtower on a different island... The creature has risen from the water. We may be able to free it if we explore the rest of its body.

side:38.text: The dragons who haunt this valley are not of these lands. They hunt the animals who lie here and must be exterminated. We should seek the creature's nest to kill it where it lives.

side:39.text: We encountered a dreki when we entered the jungle's dam. It does not look like we can reach its feeding ground while the water blocks our path. Now that we've reached the dreki's feeding ground, we must slay it. Retreat will be impossible. We should be prepared.

boss:1.text: This article contains lore based on real-life sources from Norse mythology as introduced from the God of War Norse era. Thor (Old Norse: Þórr, Nordic: ᚦᛟᚱ), also known as Thor Odinson (Translation: Thor, Son of Odin) was the Norse Aesir God of Thunder, Lightning, Storms, Wrestling, Strength, Consecration, the Sky, War, Hallowing, the Champion of the Aesir and Prince of Asgard.

boss:2.text: This article contains lore based on real-life sources from Norse mythology as introduced from the God of War Norse era. Freya (Old Norse: Freyja, Nordic: ᚠᚱᛖᛁᚨ), also known as Frigg (Old Norse: Frigga, Nordic: ᚠᚱᛁᚷᚷ), Freya Njördsdottir (Translation: Freya, Daughter of Njörd) and Nað (Nordic: ᚾᚨᛞ), is the Vanir Goddess of Love, Beauty, War, Death, Magic, Childhood and Fertility.

boss:3.text: This article contains lore based on real-life sources from Norse mythology as introduced from the God of War Norse era. Garm (Nordic: ᚵᚨᛗᛦ), also known Hróðvitnir (Nordic: ᚼᚱᚢᚦᚠᛁᛏᚾᛁᛦ) by the Aesir and Fenrir (Nordic: ᚠᛖᚾᚱᛁᚱ) after his death, was a Jötunn monstrous wolf that was imprisoned in Helheim and is the father of Sköll and Hati.

boss:4.text: This article contains lore based on real-life sources from Norse mythology as introduced from the God of War Norse era. Heimdall (Old Norse: Heimdallr, Nordic: ᚺᛖᛁᛗᛞᚨᛚᛚ), also known as Heimdall Odinson (Translation: Heimdall, Son of Odin), also famed as the Watchman of the Aesir, the Bearer of Gjallarhorn and the Herald of Ragnarök, was the Norse God of Foresight, Surveillance, Order and, Foreknowledge and Prince of…

boss:7.text: This article contains lore based on real-life sources from Norse mythology as introduced from the God of War Norse era. Odin (Old Norse: Óðinn, Nordic: ᛟᛞᛁᚾ), also known as the All-Father and Odin Borrson (Translation: Odin, Son of Borr), was the King of the Aesir and the ruler of the Norse Pantheon.
